card.title: Chosen by Power
card.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. That means I can sit at her table, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating donors. She says hello to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me again. If she remembers me, you'll know I belong there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked you to bring over that empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She picked me. I'll carry it over and ask which side of her I should sit.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes the mayor's greeting as belonging, A3 seeks remembered attention, and A5 reads a chair-carrying request as selection for proximity.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's donor seating restriction prompts A3's reintroduction; B4's chair request becomes A5's claim to a seat beside the mayor.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a seating job and B4 conveys a concrete request rather than validating A's status inference.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's instrumental attention as proof of personal inclusion at the influential table.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish a mayor's table and donor seating, making the desired access clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's which-side question transforms the actual empty-chair errand from B4 into imagined membership.
